CT417 Topic Guide

Automated Testing and Security Tooling

Explain what the tool can see, diagnose its failure, and improve feedback without weakening assurance.

What repeatedly appears in the papers

2024/25 and 2025/26 both devote a full 20-mark question to this family: SAST versus DAST, OWASP ZAP troubleshooting, SonarQube performance, and coverage-led testing. These are the highest-value current patterns on this page.

Rapid refresher

Tool/ideaExam distinction
SASTAnalyses source, bytecode or build artefacts early; finds code-pattern/data-flow issues; example: SonarQube.
DASTProbes a running authorised application, usually in staging; finds runtime/configuration behaviour; example: OWASP ZAP.
CoverageShows executed lines/branches; it identifies test gaps but does not prove good assertions or security.
Quality gateA stated threshold or policy applied to evidence; it must not become an unexplained “tool passed” claim.

How to answer tooling failures

  1. State the likely technical cause, not just the tool name.
  2. Give a fix that could be implemented in CI: readiness check, authentication context, network access, cache, report upload or test selection.
  3. For speed, state what assurance remains and what trade-off is introduced.

Practice question - security automation and coverage (20 marks)

Inspired by: 2024/25 Question 2 and 2025/26 Question 2.

(a) Compare SAST and DAST by timing, suitable vulnerabilities, source-code access, and one example tool each. [5 marks]

Model answer: SAST examines source, bytecode or build artefacts without executing the application. It runs early in development/CI and can identify code-level issues such as unsafe APIs, hard-coded secrets and suspicious data flows; SonarQube is an example. DAST attacks or probes a running application in an authorised test environment. It can reveal runtime issues such as exposed endpoints, weak headers, session/authentication behaviour and some injection behaviour; OWASP ZAP is an example. SAST needs analysable code/artefacts; DAST does not need source but needs a reachable configured target. They complement each other.

(b) OWASP ZAP fails in CI and no meaningful report is available. Identify two likely causes and a practical resolution for each. [5 marks]

Model answer: First, the target may not be healthy or reachable from the runner. Add a health check/retry and ensure the test environment/network is available before ZAP starts. Second, the scan may be unauthenticated, incorrectly scoped, or write its report to a path that is discarded. Configure an authorised test account and ZAP context/scope, then upload HTML/JSON reports as pipeline artefacts even when findings make the job fail. The answer needs both a cause and an operational fix.

(c) SonarQube creates long feedback loops. Give two improvements, explaining the benefit and trade-off of each. [5 marks]

Model answer: Cache dependencies and scanner data, and use changed-code/incremental analysis when the platform supports it. This avoids repeated work, but cache invalidation must be managed and a full scan is still needed. Also run a fast pull-request analysis with a gate for changed code, plus a full scan on main or nightly. This gives developers quick feedback while retaining broader analysis, but repository-wide findings may arrive later and need clear ownership.

(d) Payment code has low coverage. Explain how a coverage tool finds the gap and give one efficient test strategy. [5 marks]

Model answer: Run JaCoCo, Istanbul or Coverage.py in the test job and publish its line/branch report. Inspect the payment package for unexecuted decisions, especially validation, limits, authorisation and error paths. Add focused unit tests around these branches using mocks/fakes for slow gateways, while keeping only a small set of integration tests for the real boundary. This raises meaningful coverage without forcing every pull request through a slow end-to-end suite.

Final check

  • For SAST/DAST, did I compare all requested dimensions?
  • For ZAP, did I give a cause and a fix?
  • For coverage, did I avoid saying that a high percentage alone proves quality?
